correctness.rationale: For 0<α<1, Laplace representation of concave x^α makes the second differences of (n+1)^α negative; the sharp disk upper bound for Re[t/(1-u t)] gives Re Hα>0 and radial t→1 gives infimum 0. For 1<α<2, positive second differences and the disk lower bound give Re Hα>Hα(-1)=4η(-α)>0, with equality approached radially. At α=0,1,2 exact rational forms are respectively 1-t,1,(1+t)/(1-t), giving floors 0,1,0. For α>2, fixed right-half-sector polylog expansion near t=e^{-s} gives Γ(α+1)s^{1-α}; selecting arg s with cos((α-1)arg s)<0 forces inf -∞. For 2<β<=3, eta(-β)<0 and Fβ(0)>0 force a negative-real zero, while Rolle plus Li_s derivative increments β by 1, establishing real zeros for all α>2. Representative independent mpmath values and a supercritical negative real-part witness support but do not prove the continuum reasoning.

value.rationale: Weighted disk reproducing kernels and their Lu Qi-Keng zero-free range form natural complex-analysis objects. The precise Carathéodory lower envelope over all complex disk points and all real α≥0 gives sharp uniform positivity constants, the boundary minimizer transition and an exact threshold; the contribution is not merely reproducing a small zero table.

limitations: Only α>=0 and weights (n+1)^α, not arbitrary weighted Bergman spaces or count of all zeros.
Special-case zero existence is classical; full priority for continuum real-part optimization remains provisional.
